what: Fixed WebGL plate behind the screen: three big blobs of light drift very slowly in places rippled by noise (time ×.08, 4-octave noise at 1.2× scale, warped by 1.1) and blend with the background color — blob weight is (distance+.25) to the power of −2.2, −2.2, −2.4 (third ×.8), background weight 1.1. The data-glow name of the section crossing the 70% line of the screen moves the four colors (background and three blobs) with an exponential of 300ms time constant, so the whole page glow shifts slowly at each section (paper → yellow → pink → blue night → mint). Drawn at 24fps with pixel ratio × .5 resolution, and the canvas turns on over 1.2s. On top sit three layers of noise grain (.4, and 1 in the dark Skin section)

options.names: Skin names used in this section (space-separated) — for each name, this element gets --fx-glow-<Name>-0~3 css variables are set. By default the part supplies them as background · accent colors
options.attr: Skin name attribute attached to the section, default data-glow
options.line: Share of screen height for choosing a section, default .7
options.dark: Dark Skin names to thicken the noise grain (1)
options.res: Resolution multiplier for pixel ratio, default .5

use: · data-glow on the section="night"
note: The current skin name is attached to this element as data-palette and the tone as data-tone (light, dark). With reduced motion, a scene with time stopped changes immediately when it crosses a section. Without WebGL, the fallback’s three rounded gradients are shown.

from.where: index.html fixed background (original background — three shader light blobs · five skins by section data-background · 300ms exponential · 24fps · DPR×.5)
